name: Drip coffee
caffeine: Full caffeine, all from the coffee; the dose and cup size decide how much.

house.ask: Not printed on the menus as its own drink: ask at lineup how the house brews its hot coffee, by batch brewer, pour-over or press.

what: Drip coffee is filter coffee made by machine: hot water sprays over medium ground coffee in a basket and drains through paper into a pot or airpot. The trade calls it batch brew or just the pot, and it is two jobs: brewing it well, then holding it well.
taste: Even and middle of the road: medium body, clean, no single note forward. Kept on a hotplate it turns flat and drying.

steps: Rinse the airpot hot and seat a paper filter in the basket.
Weigh about 60 g of medium ground coffee per litre into the filter and level the bed; a scoop swings the ratio.
Brew the size the basket was built for, or use the half batch setting.
Run it into the sealed airpot, never onto an open hotplate, and write the brew time on it.
Read the spent grounds: level and evenly soaked, not cratered on one side and dry on the other.
Sell it within 30 to 60 minutes, and never top an old pot up with fresh.
make.ratio: About 55 to 65 g per litre, roughly 1:15 to 1:18
make.dose: About 60 g medium ground coffee to 1 litre water
make.time: 4 to 8 minute cycle; 30 to 60 minutes sealed
make.cup: Pre-heated mug or cup, 6 to 12 oz

serve: Pour from the airpot into a warmed mug or cup on a saucer with a spoon, cream and sugar as the guest takes them. Top up before the cup runs dry. It is the coffee for brunch, a banquet or a whole table at once.
story: The urn is where the coffee money is: brunch, banquets, forty cups without stopping. Guests notice age, not the machine. A hotplate keeps cooking coffee, so the aromatics leave and the acids turn harsher, flat and drying rather than weaker. A guest who says stewed is usually tasting a pot left on heat.
guest: Filter coffee is brewed through paper, so it drinks clean and even. How do you take it: cream, sugar, or black?
watch: Half a batch in a full basket runs straight through a shallow bed: thin and sour.
A guest says burnt or stewed: ask how long the pot has stood before touching the grinder.

recall.prompt: Drip coffee: how is it made?
recall.answer: About 60 g of medium ground coffee a litre, a full basket brewed through paper at 195 to 205F (90 to 96C) into a sealed airpot, poured into a warmed mug: clean, even and medium bodied.

quiz.q: Half a pot is brewed in a full-size basket on the full setting. How will it drink?
quiz.explain: The small dose makes a shallow bed that water runs straight through, under-extracting it. Use the half batch setting or the small basket.

quiz.q: What filter ratio does the Library tell you to hold?
quiz.explain: Sixty grams a litre is just under 1:17; most bars sit between 1:16 and 1:18. 18 g in, 36 g out is espresso.

quiz.q: Why does brewed coffee on an open hotplate taste worse after half an hour?
quiz.explain: Aromatics evaporate and the acids turn harsher: flat and drying, not weaker. A sealed airpot holds it longer.

video.label: How to brew drip coffee by machine
video.watchFor: The coffee weighed rather than scooped, the grind set for the filter, and the finished pot swirled before the first cup is poured. A batch brewer on a bar keeps the same rules, only larger.
